rows.text: Ral-Storm is a new Bracket 4 list because no Ral, Monsoon Mage deck existed in this owner's catalog. It starts from EDHREC's expensive shell, then adds reliable draw, protection and enough lands instead of depending on a perfect turbo hand. Ral's creature-side lost coin flips cost life: transform him before a long repeatable loop rather than calling that loop safe while he keeps dealing damage to you.

guide.title: Cost reduction, then a deliberate transformation

rows.name: Ral, Monsoon Mage
rows.text: Reduces only generic instant/sorcery costs. Every such cast on YOUR turn flips a coin; losses deal one damage to you, wins optionally transform him. You can decline a winning transformation to retain the front's discount, but cannot decline the flip or loss damage.

cards.name: Ral, Monsoon Mage // Ral, Leyline Prodigy

rows.name: Ral, Monsoon Mage
rows.text: The back starts with two loyalty plus the number of instant/sorcery spells you have cast that turn, so six such spells give eight loyalty on transformation. Resolve the current spell and clear the stack before activating a loyalty ability.

cards.name: Ral, Monsoon Mage // Ral, Leyline Prodigy

rows.name: Ral, Monsoon Mage
rows.text: After transforming, the plus-one establishes a one-generic discount until your next turn without further creature-side coin losses. The minus-eight instead grants permission to cast instant/sorcery cards among the top eight for free that turn. Choose the mode the hand actually needs; you cannot normally activate both that turn.

cards.name: Ral, Monsoon Mage // Ral, Leyline Prodigy

rows.name: Geist of Saint Thalia
rows.text: A second cost reducer that survives Ral's transformation. Its generic reduction covers noncreature spells and makes ritual/cantrip chains more reliable without requiring repeated coin-flip wins.

rows.name: Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun
rows.text: Gives your instant/sorcery spells split second. It restricts responses while one is on the stack, but does not erase triggered abilities or protect non-instant/sorcery spells. You also cannot cast your own counterspell while a split-second spell remains on the stack.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: Spells cannot be countered while Squelcher survives. The ward tax on other creatures is a cost, not immunity to removal. It does not suppress opponents' activated abilities.

rows.name: Ponder + Preordain + Brainstorm + Consider
rows.text: Reliable low-cost draw and filtering replace several awkward discard/fork slots from the seed. Make land drops, find protection, then chain into the actual engine.

rows.name: Faithless Looting
rows.text: Prepare the graveyard and keep the spells the next turn needs. Do not rely on a discarded card being recoverable without Breach or flashback; this is selection at the cost of cards, not raw card advantage.

guide.title: Rituals need an outlet, not just a large mana pool

rows.name: Rite of Flame
rows.text: A one-red start to the chain. Cost reduction cannot reduce that red pip; its extra mana counts cards with the same name in ALL graveyards, not storm copies.

rows.name: Desperate Ritual + Pyretic Ritual
rows.text: Each normally costs two and makes three red; with one generic reduction it costs one red. Desperate's splice needs another Arcane spell and the appropriate additional cost, not merely any instant.

rows.name: Seething Song
rows.text: With a one-generic reduction it costs one-red-plus-one and makes five red, setting up both ordinary chaining and the Reiterate route.

rows.name: Jeska's Will
rows.text: With a commander present, including a transformed commander, it may use both modes. Mana depends on the targeted hand. The exiled cards are temporary resources; check land-play limits and the mana needed to cast them.

rows.name: Hidden Strings + Snap
rows.text: Untap real mana sources after their other effects. Snap needs a legal creature target; if the target is illegal on resolution you do not untap lands. Strings can untap two useful permanents but its cipher requires later combat damage for more copies.

rows.name: Birgi, God of Storytelling + Electro, Assaulting Battery
rows.text: Birgi refunds red per spell and Electro per instant/sorcery cast. Electro's mana does not empty between steps. The refunds trigger on casts, not storm copies or copied rituals.

cards.name: Birgi, God of Storytelling // Harnfel, Horn of Bounty

rows.name: Storm-Kiln Artist
rows.text: Creates a Treasure for each instant/sorcery cast OR copy, so Bonus Round, Reiterate and storm all make additional mana. Resolve the triggers in a controlled order rather than overlooking the original casting payment.

rows.name: Bonus Round
rows.text: Each instant or sorcery cast afterward is copied, including opponents' spells. Copies are not cast and do not recursively trigger Bonus Round. A ritual copy can fund the next spell, but opponents may also get doubled interaction once the stack permits it.

rows.name: Reiterate + Seething Song
rows.text: With Ral TRANSFORMED and his plus-one discount active, or with Geist's one-generic reduction, buyback Reiterate costs five total and each copied Song makes five. Start with the original Song on the stack and five available mana, repeat for arbitrary storm, then resolve the original and cast Grapeshot. This is mana-neutral, not mana-positive by itself. Do not run it with creature-side Ral taking repeated loss damage.

rows.name: Reiterate + Seething Song + Birgi, God of Storytelling
rows.text: With Ral transformed, Birgi's red refund can sustain even the full six-mana buyback cost against Song's five. A further one-generic reduction makes it mana-positive. Keep enough initial mana for the first copy; refunds arrive after casting.

cards.name: Birgi, God of Storytelling // Harnfel, Horn of Bounty

rows.name: Reiterate + Jeska's Will
rows.text: With Ral transformed and no other reducer, buyback costs six. Copy Will's mana mode against a hand of at least six to sustain storm, or seven to net mana. Copies can choose another target, whose real hand size matters. Stop if the prerequisites no longer hold.

rows.name: Grapeshot
rows.text: The immediate storm-count outlet. Count opponents' actual life totals and assign enough copies to each. Infinite red mana without casts is not enough, and copying Grapeshot does not create another storm trigger.

guide.title: Breach is a funded engine, not a three-card wish

rows.name: Underworld Breach + Lion's Eye Diamond + Brain Freeze
rows.text: Resolve Breach before discarding the hand to Diamond. Escape Diamond for three other cards, make three blue, then escape Freeze for one-blue-plus-one and three other cards. Use enough mill copies on yourself to feed the next two escapes, then send surplus at opponents. Watch the shrinking library and actual fuel.

rows.name: Brain Freeze
rows.text: Milling libraries does not immediately make players lose. Follow with a draw effect when safe, a Grapeshot finish, or a controlled turn pass. Keep enough of your own library for any draw spell you intend to resolve.

rows.name: Intuition -> Lion's Eye Diamond + Brain Freeze + Past in Flames
rows.text: With Breach available and sufficient fodder, either the chosen hand card or the graveyard cards can be used. With no recovery engine, the opponent's choice means this is NOT a guaranteed one-card combo. Never hide that prerequisite.

rows.name: Past in Flames + Flashback
rows.text: Recover rituals and selection after a stalled attempt. Flashback the one-red instant can give a chosen instant/sorcery in the graveyard its own flashback permission. These permissions do not recover artifacts or enchantments and spells cast through flashback are exiled.

rows.name: Echo of Eons + Wheel of Fortune
rows.text: Eons refills and shuffles graveyards; Wheel discards and preserves graveyard fuel. Eons can undo a mill finish or remove the Breach resources you intended to use. Choose intentionally rather than taking the first available wheel.

rows.name: Timetwister + Windfall
rows.text: More reloads with different consequences. Twister shuffles graveyards and Windfall's draw count depends on the largest discarded hand. Do not claim Windfall always draws seven or will force a draw when every hand is empty.

rows.name: Mystical Tutor -> Intuition
rows.text: Top-deck access to a setup or answer, with a draw still needed. Tutor after fetches and other shuffling effects.

rows.name: Personal Tutor -> Past in Flames
rows.text: Finds a sorcery on top: recovery, a wheel, Gamble, Grapeshot or a ritual. It cannot directly find Breach, Diamond or an instant.

rows.name: Merchant Scroll -> Brain Freeze
rows.text: Blue-instant access to the mill piece, Intuition or protection in hand. It does not find the red ritual or an arbitrary enchantment.

rows.name: Gamble + Solve the Equation
rows.text: Gamble finds any card with a random-discard risk; Equation finds an instant or sorcery directly to hand. Equation does not find Breach or Diamond.

rows.name: Chrome Mox + Mox Diamond + Mox Amber + Mox Opal
rows.text: Use functioning moxen, not imagined zero-cost mana. Amber sees a legendary creature OR planeswalker, so the transformed Ral still enables it. Diamond requires a land discard and Opal requires three artifacts.

rows.name: Mana Vault + Sol Ring + Lotus Petal
rows.text: Supply the initial mana for Ral and an engine. Vault and Ring are colorless; Petal can repair a missing color but is spent afterward. Do not discard Breach to Diamond before casting it.

rows.name: Ancient Tomb + City of Traitors + Gemstone Caverns
rows.text: Fast lands help a protected attempt. Traitors sacrifices when you play another land, and Caverns needs an opening-hand, nonstarting-player condition plus an exiled card for its special start.

rows.name: Force of Will + Fierce Guardianship + Pact of Negation
rows.text: Keep the prerequisites and Pact's next-upkeep bill in mind. A transformed commander still satisfies Guardianship's commander requirement.

rows.name: Flusterstorm + Pyroblast + Red Elemental Blast
rows.text: Win the key counter fight or remove a blue permanent before committing. These do not cover every creature spell or activated ability. Split second can prevent responding while your own protected spell is on the stack.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift + Chain of Vapor + Otawara, Soaring City
rows.text: Clear resolved hate before the chain. Overloading Rift costs seven before applicable reductions; Chain may be copied by its target's controller. Otawara is a channel ability and survives many spell-counter restrictions.

The finished list has 26 true lands plus five modal spell/lands, rather than the seed's 17 true lands. Keep two functional colored sources, Ral or a reliable setup plan, and a draw/tutor or ritual chain with protection. A one-land hand whose only help is conditional Opal is a mulligan. Treat a modal land used as mana as a spell you no longer have.

Develop early, use the front discount for a few efficient spells, and transform when the loyalty or life total makes that correct. For a long Reiterate line, establish the planeswalker discount or another sustainable refund before starting; do not gamble a finite life total through an arbitrary number of flips. The normal target is a protected turn-four-or-later Bracket 4 attempt, not a claim of measured consistency or a turn-one cEDH plan.
